Frame it like two sharp handicappers/models disagreeing on a number and needing you to decide which one to trust, then dig into why (asymptotic series behavior, resummation assumptions).
discussion_why: The 'two elite methods disagree, who's right' framing maps perfectly onto line-shopping/sharp-vs-sharp disagreement culture.

title: Ising Duel: Perturbation vs. Bootstrap
paper: 2607.07776v1 — Seven- and eight-loop critical exponents of the three-dimensional Ising model

discussion_why: Playable physics toy with a built-in 'which model is right' debate baked into the UI.

title: Asymptotic Series Explorer
paper: 2607.07776v1 — Seven- and eight-loop critical exponents of the three-dimensional Ising model

discussion_why: Educational value but limited outside a physics/math audience.

title: Bandwagon Simulator: Ising Model on Random Regular Graphs
paper: 2607.07867v1 — An edge-bicolored graph approach to the Ising model on random regular graphs
pitch: Interactive network demo: generate a random d-regular graph (each node = a fan/bettor with a fixed number of connections), run Ising-style opinion dynamics (spin = 'team A' or 'team B'), and sweep a 'social temperature' slider through the paper's proven second-order phase transition — watch the network suddenly snap from disordered opinions to a mean-field-class consensus cascade. Frame as visualizing bandwagon/momentum effects in fandoms or betting-market sentiment.
discussion_why: Directly visualizes herd/momentum behavior familiar to sports and betting communities, with a genuine 'sudden flip' surprise.

title: Exact Free-Energy Solver via Edge-Bicolored Graph Counting

discussion_why: Solid research-replication value but appeals mainly to a math/physics niche.

paper: 2607.07867v1 — An edge-bicolored graph approach to the Ising model on random regular graphs

discussion_why: Popular-science framing of network contagion resonates with anyone who's watched a betting market or fanbase flip suddenly.

title: Convex but Not SOS-Convex: A Counterexample You Can Rotate
paper: 2607.23476v1 — Convexity and SOS-Convexity of Sum of Separable and Biquadratic Quartic Polynomials and Optimization

discussion_why: A real mathematical surprise (convexity outruns SOS) but the audience for caring is narrow.

title: SPBQ-Fast: Structured Quartic Optimization for Portfolio/Bankroll Construction
paper: 2607.23476v1 — Convexity and SOS-Convexity of Sum of Separable and Biquadratic Quartic Polynomials and Optimization
pitch: The paper shows SPBQ-structured quartics give 'notable computational benefits' over general SOS solvers for convex optimization. Pitch: a lightweight solver library that exploits this structure for quartic-utility bankroll/portfolio optimization (risk-of-ruin objectives with higher-order terms beyond mean-variance), sold to sports-betting and prop-trading shops wanting faster convex-regression-style position sizing than generic SDP solvers.
discussion_why: Ties a real optimization speedup to bankroll/portfolio sizing, a favorite decision-theory debate topic.

paper: 2607.23476v1 — Convexity and SOS-Convexity of Sum of Separable and Biquadratic Quartic Polynomials and Optimization

title: Loop vs. Star: The Trip-Chaining Efficiency Simulator

title: Chainable: an errand-loop nudge app

discussion_why: surprise factor — 'wait, the quantum-chaos map is literally how you shuffle cards' is a genuine wait-really moment for a poker crowd.

discussion_why: direct hit on gambling — 'is my online casino's shuffler/RNG actually random' is a perennial, heated Discord debate this gives real math ammo for.
